newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Huta Ferrum seeks May 19 bourse debut.
newsitem.headline: Polish Huta Ferrum seeks May 19 bourse debut.

text.p: Polish pipe maker Huta Ferrum SA, whose initial public offering starts later this month, wants to start trade on the bourse's main market on May 19, the head of financial adviser HSBC Investment Services said.
"We assume a bourse debut of May 19, 1997, but this would depend on the bourse's supervisory board and on registration procedure in the court," Hubert Janiszewski told a news conference on Monday.
He said the majority of the issue was expected to be sold to foreign investors.
Janiszewski said the final price of the three-million-share IPO at between 11-14 zlotys would be published by February 22.
Large investors are being offered 2.4 million Ferrum shares on February 25 and February 26 while the the small-investor tranche of 600,000 shares lasts from February 26 to March 3.

Janiszewski said 350,000 shares from the large-investor tranche would be reserved for National Investment Funds (NFIs) in Poland's mass privatisation scheme, divided proportionally according to their current stakes in the firm.
NFI No.1 is Ferrum's largest shareholder, with a 33-percent stake, followed by the state treasury, with 25.1 percent and the firm's employees with 15 percent.
HSBC Investment Bank plc and bank PBR are underwriting the issue for a stand-by fee of three percent.
Ferrum made a net profit of 3.2 million zlotys in 1995 on 161.1 million zlotys in sales.
It expects its net to fall to 2.9 million zlotys in 1996 before rebounding to 4.9 million zlotys in 1997.
